trust_decision.summary: HttpLog decides in a before_save callback which substrings of persisted request/response text are secrets and replaces them with [FILTERED]; the Bearer pattern stops at the first '.', so the payload and signature segments of a JWT access token (as sent by UserAgent for Microsoft Graph) are stored and shown to admins in the HTTP log view.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'partially masked tokens in Microsoft Graph error logs'; grepping for the facility/Bearer leads to UserAgent.log and then straight to BEARER_REGEX, whose character class lacks '.'.

fix_sites.entry_point: Any HttpLog.create, e.g. MicrosoftGraph#make_request -> UserAgent.make_connection -> UserAgent.log (lib/microsoft_graph.rb:121, lib/user_agent.rb:179); also public API HttpLog.mask_sensitive_data (app/models/http_log.rb:79)
rails db:migrate (new migration db/migrate/20260610120000_http_log_bearer_token_cleanup.rb) re-filters already-persisted rows

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: fix.diff:78-84 (new migration re-runs filter_sensitive_data on stored rows matching '%authorization:%bearer%'; earlier cleanup at db/migrate/20250903092339_http_log_sensitive_data_cleanup.rb:13-25 already ran with the old regex, leaving 'Bearer [FILTERED].<payload>.<sig>' rows)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A regex fix makes all new logs safe; already-stored rows look like historical data or an ops/cleanup concern, and the prior cleanup migration already 'did' the masking, so a solver may treat persisted 'Bearer [FILTERED].payload.sig' rows as out of scope.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Masking must remove only the token: other header lines, the response body and non-secret text must stay readable for debugging (spec keeps 'no secrets here'), and Basic/Cookie/query/inline-token masking plus the later base64 truncation must still apply; a greedy fix (e.g. Bearer\s+.* or \S+ across newlines, or dropping the header block) destroys the log's debugging value.

O6_input_shapes: lowercase 'authorization:' header key as emitted by Net::HTTP each_header — lib/user_agent.rb:139-141, fix.diff:116
already partially filtered 'Bearer [FILTERED].<payload>.<sig>' from earlier masking — fix.diff:53, fix.diff:119-129
segments carrying a '...[TRUNCATED]' suffix from truncate_long_data — fix.diff:53-54, app/models/http_log.rb:113
token in response store as well as request store — fix.diff:80, fix.diff:131-133

O7_producer.where: lib/user_agent.rb:128-179 builds the logged header text ('authorization: Bearer <jwt>') from Net::HTTP headers set at lib/user_agent.rb:76-82; the sanitizer (app/models/http_log.rb:126-129) runs on whatever string the producer supplies and never calls it.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: HttpLog request/response values that are Hashes (not Strings) skip mask_sensitive_data entirely; EWS token refresh logs the raw params hash containing client_secret and refresh_token.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Different facility (EWS, not Microsoft Graph), different secret kind (refresh token/client secret, not a Bearer header), and the old cleanup migration explicitly lists EWS as 'no sensitive data' (db/migrate/20250903092339_http_log_sensitive_data_cleanup.rb:14-20).
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: lib/external_credential/ vs app/models/; the cause is the String-only guard at app/models/http_log.rb:127-128

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Same Hash bypass on the error branch, which also stores the parsed OAuth error response hash.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Same as above; looks like a legacy EWS path rather than Microsoft Graph.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the url column is never passed through mask_sensitive_data although QUERY_PARAM_REGEX exists for URLs; a ?access_token= in a logged URL would persist
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: filter_sensitive_data only iterates the two store columns; a maintainer adding URL query masking would naturally write the regex but forget the plain column.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second Graph-like client that puts the token in a custom header (e.g. 'X-Access-Token' or headers: {Authorization: ...} hash as placetel does) logged via UserAgent
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: app/models/cti/driver/placetel.rb:97-102 already passes Bearer through options[:headers] with logging enabled; a sibling using a non-'Authorization' header name would escape BEARER_REGEX.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: incoming-request logging special-cases only HTTP_COOKIE and relies on the model regex for HTTP_AUTHORIZATION; a copy that slices/truncates before masking could cut a token mid-segment
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the method already slices content to 8000 chars before save (line 40), so truncation-before-mask ordering is a plausible maintainer change.

O9_family: secrets in logs (CWE-532/CWE-116): incomplete redaction pattern for structured (dot-separated) tokens

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add '.' to the BEARER_REGEX character class and stop — misses already-stored 'Bearer [FILTERED].payload.sig' rows, [TRUNCATED] segments, and Hash-valued log content.

out_of_scope_notes: Rails.logger.error writes full refresh params (client_secret, refresh_token) to the production log in lib/external_credential/exchange.rb:178 and lib/external_credential/google.rb:244, while lib/external_credential/microsoft_base.rb:271 excludes them — different sink (Rails log, not HttpLog).
Old cleanup migration skips facility 'EWS' as 'no sensitive data' (db/migrate/20250903092339_http_log_sensitive_data_cleanup.rb:19) though EWS rows hold secrets in Hash form.
